edits.old: When MongoTypeConversionException says Cannot cast STRING into a DoubleType, Databricks identifies a mismatch between the source value and the Spark schema, with ANSI compliance enforcing strict conversion. Its guidance is to validate and align source types; disabling ANSI can return nulls and hide invalid values. MongoDB's schemaHints option can specify known field types during inference, but it does not repair inconsistent source data. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
edits.new: When MongoTypeConversionException says Cannot cast STRING into a DoubleType, Databricks identifies a schema mismatch between the data types the Spark job expects and the actual data types in the MongoDB source, with ANSI compliance settings in Spark SQL enforcing strict type checking. Its guidance is to validate the source data and update code so data types match; disabling ANSI is a fallback that may return nulls instead of errors, reducing error visibility. MongoDB's schemaHints option specifies a partial schema of known field types to use when inferring the schema for the collection. Sources: https://kb.databricks.com/sql/job-failures-when-running-apache-spark-jobs-processing-mongodb-data ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/spark-connector/current/batch-mode/batch-read-config.md

edits.old: For reads, the current connector defaults to FAILFAST, which throws when a document does not match the expected schema; PERMISSIVE sets incompatible values to null and can store the invalid document as Extended JSON, while DROPMALFORMED ignores the document. Batch schema inference samples records, so separate document/schema parsing failures from connection and runtime errors. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

evidence.quote: `ReadConfig.ParseMode.FAILFAST`: Throws an exception when parsing a document that doesn't match the schema.

`ReadConfig.ParseMode.PERMISSIVE`: Sets fields to `null` when data types don't match the schema. To store each invalid document as an extended JSON string, combine this value with the `columnNameOfCorruptRecord` option.
`ReadConfig.ParseMode.DROPMALFORMED`: Ignores any document that doesn't match the schema. **Default:** `ReadConfig.ParseMode.FAILFAST`
When you load a Dataset or DataFrame without a schema, Spark samples the records to infer the schema of the collection.

edits.rationale: MongoDB's getting-started page gives the mongodb format for 10.0.0 and later. The MongoDB forum thread shows the Failed to find the data source: mongo error with a connector JAR reportedly installed and no stated cause. Databricks docs say third-party connectors are installed on the cluster and custom third-party Spark JARs can only be installed on dedicated compute.
